resources.string: One button on the car\'s screen that calls a service on your own Home Assistant server, such as opening the garage door. Off, nothing connects.

Puts a Home Assistant button on the car\'s dashboard. One tap calls the service below on the target below, once, and the button turns green or red to say whether Home Assistant took it. It can be turned on once the address, a token and a service are saved. Only the button press connects to your server; nothing is sent in the background.

The address you open Home Assistant at from outside your home, since the phone is usually on mobile data in the car. It must be https: Android does not allow the token to be sent over plain http. A Home Assistant Cloud address works.

Made in Home Assistant under your profile, Security, Long-lived access tokens. It is stored encrypted in this app\'s private storage, never backed up and never shown again once saved, and is sent only to the server address above. Anyone with it can control your Home Assistant, so a token for a separate, non-admin user is safer.
That is not a token: it is empty, or has spaces in it.

The Home Assistant action to call, as domain.service. For example cover.open_cover or cover.toggle for a garage door, switch.turn_on for a switch, automation.trigger for an automation, or script.turn_on for a script. Home Assistant\'s Developer tools, Actions lists them all.
The entity the service is called on, such as cover.garage_door, switch.gate_opener or automation.im_home. Several can be given, separated by commas. Leave it empty for a service that takes no target.
The server address must be an https:// address, with no user name, query or # in it.
The service must be domain.service, such as cover.open_cover.
Each target must be an entity id, such as cover.garage_door.
Asks your server whether the address and token work, whether the service exists and whether each target is an entity it knows. It only reads: nothing is opened, switched or triggered.
